instructions: Read the supplied diagnostic report, then explicitly adopt, defer or reject using design.respond_diagnosis. A recommendation for future matched verification will be recorded only; no backend comparison is authorized in this stage. Choose a single recommendation only when justified. A saved-evidence response is followed by a diagnostic check phase; a recommendation may be deferred pending that check. No physical design changes or tuning.

acceptance_criteria: Model-authored request explicitly grants retained reads and one bounded saved-state numerical check.
Initial report separates exact selected facts, hypotheses and evidence gaps; design records a legal disposition.
Model chooses unresolved question, saved state/input, operation, model, horizon and bounded work; executor validates request scope before execution.
Revised report links previous report and feedback, cites exact numerical result selectors when available, and explains support/weakening/unresolved with model and horizon limits.
Final design response links the revised report; no subsequent comparison or physical improvement is evaluated.
protocol.reading: At most two successful read turns per evidence phase; a sequential batch counts once, each tool is charged. Corrections count as attempts, not reads.
protocol.scope: One saved-state check; no full backend simulation, controller tuning or physical change.

missing_evidence: No historical optimizer iterations or full warm plans are reconstructed; the retained capability list records update:30:complete_warm_and_plans and update:34:complete_warm_and_plans as missing.
Only updates 30 and 34 have matched one-step prediction-versus-measurement comparisons, so 33 of 35 updates contribute no comparison of projected versus recorded endpoint motion.
full_snapshots_available = false and snapshot_id is null for updates 30 and 34, so no retained full-backend state exists for a state-level comparison.
No retained measurement links wall-clock update cost or deadline misses to simulated-time tip motion, so any coupling between real-time feasibility and sampled settling is untested.
No retained data records per-channel tension versus the 8 N force_limit_n, so actuator-limit binding as a contributor to the late speed profile is untested.

No retained record of the last 0.05 s objective terms or tip-speed weights explains why the trajectory was still fast at run end, so the settling miss cannot yet be split between plant settling time and commanded input.

recommendations.rationale: Defer: the single bounded saved-state check that best discriminates among the remaining explanations is a prediction_braking / local_comparison probe from the saved state of the last recorded update (update 34, t = 0.34 s) with model.gvs@1.0.0, horizon_s = 0.01, implicit_euler with integration_step_s = 0.002, comparing predicted tip speed and position decay under (a) the recorded applied tensions and (b) a held or braking input against the recorded t = 0.35 endpoint. Predicted speed decaying to near zero under held input would point to late-run commanded inputs that keep injecting tip speed; predicted speed persisting would point to a plant or actuator settling timescale longer than the 0.05 s window. The probe would be bounded analysis only and would not authorise adoption of any parameter.

Defer any change to holding_tip_speed_weight or terminal_tip_speed_weight (both 0.0 in the sealed configuration): no retained selector links either weight to the late speed overshoot or to the deadline misses, so a control-parameter change is not supported by this evidence and should be sequenced after the bounded check plus a separate matched design adoption.

attribution.reason: The final 0.05 s window records tip speeds of 0.86-1.58 m/s and a terminal speed of 0.635 m/s against a 0.02 m/s limit while the position error decays to 0.0076 m inside the 0.01 m tolerance, so the observed secondary failure is a tip-speed settling miss at the end of the 0.35 s run rather than a reach miss.

Every one of the 35 updates missed the 0.01 s deadline; mean_update_s = 17.075 s and the two recorded updates spend 2.89-6.75 s in optimization and 0.35-1.64 s in warm preparation with 3.45 s and 8.59 s total update wall time.

At update 30 the recorded measured tip speed 1.3295 m/s exceeds the projected 1.1907 m/s with vector difference 0.1534 m/s, whereas update 34 differs by only 0.0185 m/s; this single high-speed comparison is consistent with the projected model under-anticipating approach speed but two samples do not establish a contribution to the late speed overshoot.

For both aligned comparisons applied_input_difference_n = 0.0 and returned/selected constraint violations are only 9.38e-06 and 9.26e-09, so recorded requested-versus-applied tension mismatch does not account for the observed endpoint differences; this rule-out is limited to the two recorded updates.

Retained evidence records deadline misses and simulated tip motion in separate domains with no measurement linking them, and the supplied scheduling semantics states wall-clock deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time; no coupling in either direction is established by the retained selectors.

facts.statement: The saved summary reports three separate outcomes for candidate proposal_compliant_build: reach_passed = true with terminal_error_m = 0.007642608585867386 m inside reach_tolerance_m = 0.01 m; sampled_settling_passed = false against settling_criteria position_limit_m = 0.01 m and speed_limit_m_s = 0.02 m/s over a 0.05 s window; and deadline_misses = 35 with mean_update_s = 17.075238151415917 s against control_period_s = 0.01 s.

Late sampled motion shows the tip error falling monotonically from 0.05813810428573256 m at t = 0.3 s to 0.007642608585867386 m at the final sample, while tip speed rises to 1.5810152739742807 m/s at t = 0.33 s and is still 0.6351726092425104 m/s at the end of the 0.35 s run, far above speed_limit_m_s = 0.02 m/s.

Recorded per-update timing for update 30 (t = 0.3 s) and update 34 (t = 0.34 s): update_wall_s = 8.590574299916625 s and 3.4527177999261767 s, optimization_solve_s = 6.753986699972302 s and 2.885958099970594 s, warm_preparation_s = 1.6389210999477655 s and 0.34554179990664124 s, both plans accepted; update 30 selection status is User_Requested_Stop with policy_stop_reason relative_seed_improvement and update 34 is Solve_Succeeded; run-level stopping_counts record User_Requested_Stop = 34 and Solve_Succeeded = 1.

Aligned one-step comparison under matching recorded interval input shows small but nonzero endpoint disagreement: tip_difference_m = 0.006240614340723002 m at update 30 and 0.001183439178222365 m at update 34; at update 30 the recorded measured tip speed 1.32948286853263 m/s exceeds the projected predicted speed 1.1906688811878083 m/s with velocity vector difference norm 0.1534294782532689 m/s, while update 34 differs by 0.018534244890083693 m/s; applied_input_difference_n = 0.0 and returned constraint violations are 9.380295274037664e-06 and 9.259625741801307e-09 in both comparisons.

gates.reason: Terminal tip speed, and late speeds up to 1.581 m/s, exceed the 0.02 m/s settling limit inside the 0.05 s window.
All 35 control updates missed the 0.01 s deadline.

limitations: No historical optimizer iterations or full warm plans are reconstructed; the retained capability lists update:30:complete_warm_and_plans and update:34:complete_warm_and_plans as missing.
full_snapshots_available = false and snapshot_id is null for updates 30 and 34, so no full backend state is retained for them.
Only updates 30 and 34 carry matched one-step prediction-versus-measurement comparisons; the other 33 updates have none, and causal_identification is listed as unsupported.
A single execution with model comparisons at two updates does not establish a dominant cause for either the settling failure or the deadline misses.
The statement that wall-clock deadline misses inject no physical delay into simulated time is supplied Human-owned scheduling context, not a retained measurement.
recommended_actions: Keep reach, sampled settling and real-time feasibility as separate outcomes; the deadline misses are a wall-clock result and must not be read as evidence about simulated tip motion.
Defer every controller or configuration change until the single bounded saved-state check is executed and its receipt is reviewed.
Do not request the numerical check in this phase; schedule it as the one permitted saved-state check (max_checks = 1, model.gvs@1.0.0, horizon_s 0.01, implicit_euler with integration_step_s 0.002).
